A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Decoding-based Regression by the same authors. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original curve-fitting, tabular regression, density-estimation, and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and reports additional regression-head comparisons in Figures 4, 6, and 13.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same normalized and sign/exponent/mantissa tokenizations, autoregressive Transformer head, cross-entropy training, sampling procedures, and repetition-based error correction. Expanded explanations and proposed future extensions do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same synthetic functions, BBOB tasks, AMLB and OpenML-CTR23 benchmarks, 25 UCI datasets, and synthetic density shapes. One-dimensional BBOB results remain in Appendix A.2 despite their omission from v2's summary table. Modern LLM and multi-objective applications remain discussion topics.

E2.justification: Figure 4 expands from the unnormalized decoder and pointwise head to include the normalized decoder and Riemann head. The OpenML Kendall-Tau comparison likewise expands to four heads in v2 Figures 6 and 13. Comparator membership in the BBOB and UCI comparisons is retained.

E3.justification: Figure 4 changes its reported training budget from unlimited points in v1 to 100K points in v2. This is a revised experimental setting description, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Existing benchmark metrics, validation settings, and optimization budgets are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: The six-function case study in Figure 4 now examines Riemann and normalized-decoder behavior, extending the evidence about failures around abrupt changes and asymptotes. The data-scaling, decoder-size, repetition, Hamming-tokenization, and density-sampling analyses remain substantively unchanged.

E5.justification: The existing ten-run averaging, ten train-test splits, standard-deviation tables, and plotted uncertainty practices are retained. Neither version adds a new significance-testing, confidence-interval, or seed-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds normalized-decoder and Riemann Kendall-Tau results and expands the Figure 4 curves, including reporting an out-of-range Riemann prediction for the tangent example. The original two-head OpenML scores and all full UCI table values are unchanged. These additions do not establish improved performance under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 replaces v1's approximate risk expression with a stated expansion containing an O(2^(-4k)+1/N) remainder and an explicit twice-continuous-differentiability assumption. Appendix B substantially rewrites the bias and variance derivations. Binary positional weights and bin-midpoint expressions are also corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies its comparison from traditional regression approaches to standard pointwise heads and changes arbitrary distributions to smooth numeric distributions. The central contributions—formalizing numeric decoding and demonstrating competitive regression and density estimation—remain intact.

C2.justification: New Section 5 identifies substantive applicability limits involving modern LLM architectures, non-digit vocabularies, sampling constraints, intermediate language generation, and reinforcement-learning training. It also develops the multi-objective extension beyond v1's brief prospect. Discussion of stochastic, Bayesian, and energy-based alternatives largely relocates existing Appendix C material.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies uniform input sampling for Figure 4 and identifies a one-layer, 32-unit decoder in the general experimental description. However, both experimental-details appendices retain the same two decoder-size options, leaving their allocation unclear. Hyperparameter sweeps, hardware, runtime, and data-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Akhauri et al. (2025), Chiang et al. (2025), Kingma and Welling (2014), and Zhang et al. (2024), including a distinction from VAE decoders. It replaces the Hollmann et al. (2023) classification reference with the 2025 tabular foundation-model work. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The introduction and regression-head taxonomy are substantially rewritten, the standalone preliminaries are folded into the method introduction, and definitions are separated from Theorem 1. A new main-text discussion incorporates former appendix material, while the conclusion is streamlined. These changes substantially reorganize the explanation without replacing the method.

P2.justification: v2 adds paired scatter plots and four-head benchmark bars, expands Figure 4's curves and legend, and reformats the BBOB summary as Table 1. Task-index labels and captions are clarified. Most existing figures and tables retain their visual structure, with relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: Fuller comparator reporting and Section 5's concrete applicability limits improve the paper's evidential completeness and scope. The central method and empirical findings remain unchanged. The theoretical rewrite fixes formulas, but its stronger remainder claim is not fully justified: Appendix B cancels a cross-term by treating a variable Taylor remainder as constant. This limits the overall gain.
